equations: F = -sum_i p_i n_i A_i (n into the fluid, from the owning tetrahedron)
assumptions: node pressures averaged to triangle centroids (SU2 uses the same nodal dual-area idea, so small differences are expected)

assumptions: far-field kinetic-energy form; streamwise perturbation neglected

independent_check.method: CL^2/(pi e AR) with AVL's span efficiency

claims.status_reason: Trefftz 0.0097 on the plane 0.3 m behind the wing TE vs CL^2/(pi e AR) 0.0095 (+1 %); planes further aft read 0.0089, 0.0080 as the trailing vortices dissipate on the tetrahedra, so the value depends on where it is measured
limitations: numerical dissipation of the trailing vortices before the plane

claims.claim: At the wall spacing of the 3-D meshes, the SU2 scheme reproduces the inviscid lift of the wing section.
equations: same SU2 INC_EULER numerics as run_cases.CFG on a 2-D gmsh mesh of the same NACA 2415 section
assumptions: 2-D section behaviour carries over to the 3-D wing's chordwise resolution
claims.ran_evidence: SU2 and XFOIL run by analysis/cfd3d/scheme_check_2d.py (2000+ iterations per case)
claims.status_reason: at the L1/L2 wall spacing the section lift slope is -19 / -14 % against XFOIL inviscid; it closes to -5 % at 603 wall edges. Numerical dissipation at this resolution acts like viscous decambering, which explains most of the 3-D lift-slope gap to AVL (CFD-05): absolute lift from the 3-D runs is mesh-limited
claims.next_step: Re-mesh the wing, tail and fins at about 2 mm wall spacing (about 300 wall edges per section) and re-run alpha 0, 4, 8; keep the other parts at the current sizes.
